children: Chicago soybean futures slid on Wednesday for the first time in four sessions, with rapidly advancing Brazilian planting adding pressure on prices, while wheat fell for a second session and corn lost ground.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-active soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
lost 0.4% to $12.29 a bushel, as of 0108 GMT. Wheat
fell 0.3% to $5.87-1/4 a bushel and corn
gave up 0.3% to $4.49-1/4 a bushel.

* Brazilian farmers had planted 86% of the projected area of their 2026/27 soybean crop as of last Thursday, agribusiness consultancy AgRural said on Monday, up from 78% a week earlier and above 81% at the same time last year.
* Rapidly advancing planting in Brazil, the world's No. 1 exporter of the oilseed, is raising expectations of global supplies for early next year.
* The soybean market was supported earlier this week by higher demand for US soymeal.

* Deforestation rules going into effect in the European Union in late December could steer soymeal export demand toward US supplies, analysts said, although a late postponement of EU rules is possible.
* The US Department of Agriculture rated 54% of the US winter wheat crop as being in good-to-excellent condition in a weekly report on Monday, up from 53% last week.
* Russian wheat export prices spiked last week following the trilateral summit of presidents Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen, analysts said.
MARKET NEWS
* Wall Street retreated on Tuesday, with tech stocks giving back some of the Monday rally sparked by Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia as CEO, while the dollar slipped.
